'''Ivan Smith''' (born 1973) {{Post-nominals|country=GBR|FRS}} is a British mathematician who deals with [[symplectic manifold]]s and their interaction with [[algebraic geometry]], [[low-dimensional topology]], and dynamics. He is a professor at the [[University of Cambridge]].

==Education and career==

Smith was born in 1973 as the second child of [[Neil Smith (linguist)|Neil Smith]], a professor of [[linguistics]] at [[University College London]], and Saras Smith. He studied at the [[University of Oxford]], where he received his doctorate in 1999 under the supervision of [[Simon Donaldson]]  with thesis ''Symplectic Geometry of Lefschetz Fibrations''.<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id = 93811|name=Ivan Smith}}</ref> Smith is now a professor in Cambridge at Gonville & Caius College.

Among other things, Smith derived nodal invariants from [[symplectic geometry]].

He received in 2007 the [[Whitehead Prize]] for his work in symplectic topology (highlighting the breadth of applied techniques from algebraic geometry and topology)<ref>[https://www.lms.ac.uk/sites/lms.ac.uk/files/About_Us/news/2007-7%20LMS%20Prizes%20(22%20June).pdf Whitehead Prize to Smith 2007]</ref> and in 2013 the [[Adams Prize]]. In 2018 he was an invited speaker at the [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] in Rio de Janeiro.

Smith was elected a [[Fellow of the Royal Society]] in 2023.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Ivan Smith |url=https://royalsociety.org/people/ivan-smith-25021/ |access-date=2023-05-25 |website=royalsociety.org}}</ref>
